question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{7x+y}{x}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{7x+(vx)}{x} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=7+v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=7 \\ \frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{7}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int\mathrm{d}v&=7\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ v&=7\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{x}&=7\ln|x|+C \\ y&=7x\ln|x|+Cx\end{aligned}
$$



The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$.

question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{-2x^3+y^3}{xy^2}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{-2x^3+(vx)^3}{x(vx)^2} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{-2+v^3}{v^2}=\frac{-2}{v^2}+v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{-2}{v^2} \\ v^2\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{-2}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int v^2\,\mathrm{d}v&=-2\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \frac{v^3}{3}&=-2\ln|x|+C_1 \\ v^3&=-6\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^3&=-6\ln|x|+C \\ y^3&=x^3(-6\ln|x|+C) \\ y&=x\sqrt[3]{-6\ln|x|+C}\end{aligned}
$$

Here $C=3C_1$ and the cube root is real. Restrict the solution to intervals where $y\ne0$.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$ and $y\ne0$.

question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{4x^3+y^3}{xy^2}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{4x^3+(vx)^3}{x(vx)^2} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{4+v^3}{v^2}=\frac{4}{v^2}+v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{4}{v^2} \\ v^2\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{4}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int v^2\,\mathrm{d}v&=4\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \frac{v^3}{3}&=4\ln|x|+C_1 \\ v^3&=12\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^3&=12\ln|x|+C \\ y^3&=x^3(12\ln|x|+C) \\ y&=x\sqrt[3]{12\ln|x|+C}\end{aligned}
$$

Here $C=3C_1$ and the cube root is real. Restrict the solution to intervals where $y\ne0$.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$ and $y\ne0$.

question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{-4x+y}{x}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{-4x+(vx)}{x} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=-4+v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=-4 \\ \frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{-4}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int\mathrm{d}v&=-4\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ v&=-4\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{x}&=-4\ln|x|+C \\ y&=-4x\ln|x|+Cx\end{aligned}
$$



The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$.

question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{6x+2y}{x}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{6x+2(vx)}{x} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=6+2v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=6+v \\ \frac{1}{6+v}\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int\frac{1}{6+v}\,\mathrm{d}v&=\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \ln|v+6|&=\ln|x|+C_1 \\ |v+6|&=e^{C_1}|x| \\ v+6&=Cx \\ v&=Cx-6\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{x}&=Cx-6 \\ y&=Cx^2-6x\end{aligned}
$$

The signed constant $C$ absorbs $e^{C_1}$. Division by $v+6$ excluded $v=-6$; restoring it permits $C=0$, giving $y=-6x$.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$.
